ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section P: Social Media and Activism From the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge to #blacklivesmatter, activism has become a regular part of the social media experience. But for every hashtag that rises to prominence, thousands perish ignominiously, and even the most viral of spreads can fail to bring about substantive change in our world. So, what constitutes an effective social-media advocacy campaign? And, how can you create one? In this course, we will explore how to communicate your world-changing ideas effectively and memorably using the various affordances of social media. We will examine how campaigns have leveraged platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, tumblr, and YouTube, and what possibilities might be left unexplored. We will look at the rhetorical potential of online texts like the selfie and videos, and we will unpack terms like ?clickbait? and ?slacktivism.? And because social media is not just about words, we will also build skills in more visual modes of communication, such as infographics, GIFs, and shareable images. Tech savvy is not a prerequisite for this course, but be prepared to exercise both your analytical and your creative sides. Graded assignments will include analyses of existing campaigns and the development of your own, as well as blog posts , image creation, and more.
